_readme: TLV-CORPUS-1 — the real-TikTok recognition corpus. Data only; the harness that runs it is
tests/manual/tiktok-recognition.manual.ts. Nothing in this file is code, and adding a URL
never requires touching the harness.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every recognition number we have (7/14 top-1) comes from
docs/evidence/places/benchmark-spec.json, whose queries were written by hand and are
script-matched to the index by construction: a Latin query for a Latin-named row. Real captions
are not. 64% of the loaded index is Hebrew-named with zero aliases, so the synthetic benchmark
systematically understates the dominant failure mode. This corpus is measured on the hard case.
WHAT TO PUT IN IT. 20-30 real TikToks representative of our users — people in their 20s in Tel
Aviv and Hasharon looking for trendy places. The six target categories, and a corpus should
cover all six:
1. cafes
2. brunch
3. bars_and_wine_bars
4. bakeries
5. desserts
6. talked_about_restaurants
Mix scripts on purpose: Hebrew captions, English captions, and captions that mix the two. A
corpus of Latin-only captions would reproduce exactly the blind spot this file exists to close.
HOW TO ADD ONE. Append an object to `cases`. Only `url` and `category` are required:
{ "url": "https://www.tiktok.com/@handle/video/1234", "category": "cafes" }
A case with no `expected` still runs, still prints its caption, its extracted candidates, and
the resolver's top-3 with names, addresses and coordinates — but it is reported as
UNADJUDICATED and counts toward neither the numerator nor the denominator of the auto-match
rate. That is deliberate: a verdict needs a rule, not a vibe. Read the run record, decide what
the caption should have resolved to, then come back and fill in `expected`.
`expected` is a LIST, because one caption can name several venues. Each entry:
name             required. The venue as a human would name it. Prose, for the report.
area             required. Street/neighbourhood, for the report. Not matched on unless you
also give addressPattern.
candidatePattern optional regex, applied to normalise(candidate.rawName). It answers 'which
extracted candidate is this expectation about?'. Defaults to a literal
match on normalise(name). An expectation that matches no candidate is an
EXTRACTION miss, and is counted as one.
namePattern      optional regex, applied to normalise(top1.name). It answers 'did the
resolver return the right venue?'. Defaults to candidatePattern.
addressPattern   optional regex, applied to `address_line + ' ' + locality` raw (not
normalised). Add it ONLY when the index really holds several distinct venues
of this name and the branch matters — otherwise a legitimate second branch
scores as a failure. Same rule as the synthetic benchmark's TLV-06/TLV-07.
indexProbe       optional list of strings ILIKE-searched against poi_index.name_norm. This is
what separates 'absent from the index' from 'present but unreachable across
scripts' — the TLV-13 failure. Give BOTH scripts where you know them.
Regexes are matched case-insensitively after normalise(), which lowercases, strips punctuation
and diacritics, and keeps Hebrew. Write them lowercase.
COST. Every oEmbed response and every extraction is cached to
docs/evidence/.local/tiktok-recognition-cache/ (gitignored) on first run and reused after. A
re-run of a 30-URL corpus costs ZERO LLM calls. Adding a URL costs exactly one.

cases.notes: The only real Tel Aviv TikTok with cached evidence in the repo as of 2026-08-27. Caption recorded in docs/handoff-2026-08-27-place-recognition.md §2.2 as 'Resturants in Tel Aviv 📍Ha Kosem' — note the misspelled 'Resturants' and the space in 'Ha Kosem', both of which are exactly the kind of thing the synthetic benchmark never contains. Imported by hand in a browser at 1280x720 and 375x812; the saved row was read back in psql and sat 11 m from the venue against 555 m and 483 m for the two model guesses.

expected.name: HaKosem
expected.addressPatternNote: Transliteration added 2026-08-28. The pattern was authored against Overture, which writes this street in Hebrew; Google returns "Shlomo HaMelekh Street 1" for the same venue at the same point. Both denote שלמה המלך 1, so accepting either keeps the guard (it still rejects a same-name venue on a different street) while no longer testing which provider answered.

expected.addressPatternNote: Second street added 2026-08-28, on measurement rather than assumption. Overture files this venue at איינשטיין 69 and Google at בארט 2; the two points are 11 m apart, i.e. the same building addressed from two streets. Accepting either is what makes this expectation about the venue rather than about a dataset's street-labelling convention.
